Event overview

As a GP or primary care worker, you may be the first person to offer help to a patient with addiction. This conference can prepare you to start and support patients’ journeys from harm reduction to recovery with confidence.

 

Join us either in Birmingham or online for a two-day conference which has been supporting primary care for over 30 years. Learn and network with hundreds of addiction healthcare professionals from across the UK and beyond.




It's the UK's leading, largest, and longest standing conference on managing addictions in primary care, delivered in partnership with Addiction Professionals.




Learn from experts

The conference chairs - Kate Halliday of Addiction Professionals and Dr Jennie Rankine MRCGP - will be joined by a raft of experts in the field of substance and behavioural addiction across the two days.

 

There will be plenaries and workshops that offer the best guidance no matter your experience level. You’ll find beginner’s guides as well as more specialist advice, from holistic care approaches to specific guidance on substances, to government policy and nationwide strategy.




Who attends

At this national conference you can find guidance for GPs, shared care workers, nurses and all primary care staff, as well as specialists, commissioners and researchers.




A discount is available if you are currently a GP or other healthcare professional in training. If you are not a member of the RCGP, please contact us with proof of trainee status to claim your discount.




Early bird discount until Thursday 3 December

Book your place early to secure a discounted ticket, available for a limited time.




Call for examples of good practice

Have you recently developed a service? Overcome a local problem and/or improved practice? Perhaps you've undertaken research or a service quality improvement audit? Or even produced educational and training materials in a film or other media?

 

Share your work with primary care workers across the UK and submit a poster, paper or film on any aspect of working with addiction primary care.

 

Click here to download the submission form.




Expert learning. By GPs, for GPs.
